name: Sigiriya Rock Fortress
description: A 5th-century rock fortress built by King Kashyapa, rising 200 m above the surrounding plains and famous for its ancient frescoes and water gardens.

name: Ella
description: A hill-country village known for hiking trails, tea estates and the Nine Arches Bridge, reached by one of the world's most scenic train rides.

name: Galle Fort
description: A 17th-century Dutch walled town on the south coast, with cobbled streets, a lighthouse, boutique shops and sunset walks along the ramparts.

name: Mirissa Beach
description: A curved bay of golden sand with calm water for swimming, whale-watching boat trips from November to April, and a lively beach café scene.

name: Yala National Park
description: Sri Lanka's most famous national park, with the highest density of leopards in the world, plus sloth bears, elephants and coastal lagoons.

name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
description: The golden-roofed temple in Kandy that houses a relic of the Buddha's tooth, and the centre of the spectacular Esala Perahera procession each July.

name: Nuwara Eliya
description: The cool hill station at 1,868 m, surrounded by tea plantations, waterfalls and the pine forests of Victoria Park, often called Little England.

name: Arugam Bay
description: A laid-back east-coast surf town with a long point break, palm-shaded beach cafés and the best surfing season in the country from April to October.

name: Minneriya National Park
description: Home of the famous elephant gathering, where up to 300 wild elephants come to the ancient Minneriya tank in the dry season between July and October.

name: Unawatuna Beach
description: A sheltered crescent bay near Galle with calm turquoise water, coral reefs for snorkelling and a long line of beach restaurants.
